title: Linearity and triangulated compatibility of normalized integral pullback
statement: Fix l prime and E/Q_l finite. Let h:W→X be a morphism of Noetherian finite-dimensional schemes with l invertible in global sections on both. Given a normalized integral/completed comparison c of [lem-a1-integral-pullback-completed-comparison], the specified ambient integralDerivedPullback is additive. For every a in O_E and morphism f:K→L of integral constructible objects in the adic presentation, its image of scalar multiplication by a followed by coefficient transport of f is scalar multiplication by a on the pulled object followed by the pulled morphism. With exactly c.derivedShift it takes every distinguished triangle whose vertices are sfIntegralConstructible to a distinguished triangle. The charts and normalization conventions are [def-a1-integral-stratum-chart-restrictions-data]. This asserts no existence of charts or preservation of constructibility.

proof.text: Finally use [lem-a1-integral-pullback-completed-comparison] for $h$ to identify the specified $Lh^*$ on derived-complete objects with the strict-tower completed pullback. It is an $R$-linear comparison. By [lem-cbc-completed-pullback-triangles], the latter has coherent integer-shift isomorphisms and preserves distinguished triangles of derived-complete objects with that shift comparison. Transport its shift comparison through $\gamma_h$: the comparison for $K[r]$ followed by the completed shift map followed by $\gamma_{h,K}[r]^{-1}$ is the shift map for the specified $Lh^*$, by the shift clause of the first cited lemma. Naturality then identifies the last arrow of the image of a triangle with the transported last arrow, so the specified functor preserves distinguished triangles. Its $R$-linearity can also be read on representatives: finite-coefficient inverse image, product, the transition map $1-s$, and both coordinates of the shifted cone commute with multiplication by every $r\in R$. Step 7 ensures that this is a functor between the integral constructible subcategories, rather than just the ambient derived-complete categories.
